method: Generic public web searches only (no repo content/paths/hostnames sent). Figures taken from paper abstracts/HTML excerpts surfaced by search; full tables NOT opened unless stated. All numbers are AUTHOR-REPORTED on public benchmarks unless marked otherwise; none reproduced on ODG hardware. Licenses marked UNVERIFIED were not checked against the LICENSE file.

signals.title: Agentless: fixed localize -> repair -> validate pipeline (no agent loop)
signals.claim: Hierarchical localization (file -> class/function -> edit location), multiple candidate patches, filtering by reproduction/regression tests and re-ranking. SWE-bench Lite 27.33% (v1, $0.34/issue) -> 32.00% (v2, 96/300, $0.70/issue) with GPT-4o-class models. A later paper (BLAgent) swapping in a better localizer raised Agentless to 38.3% (115/300) and concluded accurate file localization is necessary but not sufficient.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported on public benchmark; frontier backbone, not 7B)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes - deterministic staged pipeline with short, bounded prompts suits weak models better than open-ended tool loops; but no published 7B-backbone number found
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: localize (hierarchical narrowing before generate), select (test-filtered re-ranking); fits as stages inside ODG native loop, not a new orchestrator
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - ODG loop already has generate/test/repair; the missing measurable stage is hierarchical localization and test-filtered candidate ranking
signals.risks: Backbone was GPT-4o/Claude; 7B localization accuracy likely much lower. SWE-bench Lite has known flawed instances (authors built Lite-S).

signals.title: Repeated sampling (best-of-n) with test-based selection - Large Language Monkeys
signals.claim: Coverage on SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct rose from 15.9% (1 sample) to 56% (250 samples); 5 samples of the cheaper model beat single samples of GPT-4o/Claude 3.5 Sonnet at >3x lower cost. Gains require a verifier (unit tests) to pick the answer; coverage != selected accuracy.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (coverage/pass@k; selection gap explicitly acknowledged)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes in principle - the cheap-model+many-samples regime is exactly the small-model case; on CPU the binding constraint is tokens/sec, so n is small (e.g. 3-8) rather than 250
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: generate (n diverse candidates, ODG diversity schedule) + select (run sandbox tests, keep passing/most-agreeing)
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - directly extends ODG's diversity schedule; turns bounded repair budget into parallel samples
signals.risks: Coverage numbers overstate what is achievable without an oracle; weak/self-written tests make selection unreliable. CPU throughput limits n.

signals.title: CodeT: dual execution agreement with model-generated tests
signals.claim: Same model generates candidate solutions and tests; candidates clustered by which tests they pass and ranked by (tests passed x cluster size). HumanEval pass@1 47.0% -> 65.8% and MBPP 58.1% -> 67.7% (code-davinci-002); APPS-intro 27.2% -> 34.6%. Failure mode: correct solution generated but not top-ranked in 53/164 HumanEval problems (cushman-001).
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported; function-level benchmarks, older models)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes - pure inference-time selection, no training; tested across 5 models incl. smaller ones (exact small-model gains not extracted)
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: select (rank candidates when no trusted test exists or as tie-breaker); test (generate extra tests)
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - cheap selector for the candidates ODG already produces; useful when only partial tests exist
signals.risks: Self-generated tests are biased (see C-06); agreement rewards consistent-but-wrong clusters; function-level gains may not transfer to repo-level tasks.

signals.title: Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet? (budget-normalized self-repair)
signals.claim: When repair cost is counted, gains are modest, vary across subsets and are sometimes absent; i.i.d. sampling without repair often matches or beats repair at small budgets. Bottleneck is the model's ability to give feedback on its own code; feedback from a stronger model or humans helps substantially. Recommendation: spend more budget on diverse initial samples than on deep repair.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (HumanEval/APPS with Code Llama, GPT-3.5, GPT-4)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes - directly informative: Code Llama (small open model) was among tested models; implies 7B self-feedback is the weak link
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: repair budget allocation (wide-then-shallow) and optional feedback-from-stronger-model at repair stage
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - a calibration warning for ODG's bounded repair: measure pass@budget for 'n samples' vs 'k samples + repair' before assuming repair helps
signals.risks: Older models; results on competitive/function-level tasks.

signals.title: Self-Debugging (execution feedback + explanation)
signals.claim: Each turn: generate -> execute -> model explains code -> revise. Authors claim it matches or outperforms baselines that generate >10x more candidates (sample efficiency) and reached SOTA on several code benchmarks at the time.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured by authors; exact numbers NOT extracted in this collection (UNVERIFIED here)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: unknown - shown with large models; C-04 and C-06 suggest small models benefit less from self-feedback
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: repair (add 'explain-then-fix' prompt using sandbox stdout/stderr/trace)
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - ODG already repairs with execution feedback; the explanation step is a cheap prompt change to A/B
signals.risks: Gains depend on real (not self-generated) tests; contradicted at small budgets by C-04.

signals.title: Revisit Self-Debugging with Self-Generated Tests (post- vs in-execution)
signals.claim: Post-execution self-debugging against self-written tests struggles on HumanEval/MBPP because test bias produces misleading feedback; in-execution debugging (reasoning over intermediate runtime states, not pass/fail labels) reduces the bias and was effective across models on LiveCodeBench.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (frontier models; small-model results NOT confirmed)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: unknown - not shown for 7B
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: repair (feed variable/trace snapshots from sandbox rather than only assertion failures); test (treat self-generated tests as low-trust)
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - governance-relevant: self-generated tests must not be the acceptance oracle
signals.risks: Trace capture adds sandbox complexity; language-specific instrumentation.

signals.title: Reflexion: verbal reinforcement (lesson memory across attempts)
signals.claim: Converts environment feedback (e.g., failed tests) into textual self-reflections stored in episodic memory for the next attempt; reported 91% pass@1 on HumanEval vs 80% for GPT-4 baseline; intro says up to 11% improvement on Python tasks (different baselines).
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (GPT-4 backbone); HumanEval is saturated/contaminated so headline is weak evidence
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: unknown/doubtful - relies on quality of self-reflection, the weak point for small models (C-04)
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: repair + memory (ODG lesson store already exists: persist reflection keyed by failure signature)
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - conceptually already present in ODG lesson stores; value is in measuring whether stored lessons raise pass rate
signals.risks: Wrong reflections get persisted and reused (memory poisoning); HumanEval leakage.

signals.title: AlphaCodium flow engineering (test-driven multi-stage flow)
signals.claim: Problem reflection -> public-test reasoning -> generate AI tests -> iterate code against public+AI tests. GPT-4 pass@5 on CodeContests validation 19% -> 44%; gain also reported for open DeepSeek model.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported; validation set, 107 vs 117 problem count inconsistency between paper and README)
signals.license: AGPL-3.0 (Codium-ai/AlphaCodium) - UNVERIFIED; if AGPL, reuse ideas not code
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: unknown - many LLM calls per problem; on CPU cost is latency
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: plan (problem reflection) + test (AI-generated tests anchored by real tests) + repair
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - validates 'structured flow > single prompt'; ODG already has a flow
signals.risks: Competitive-programming domain; license may restrict code reuse; validation-set result.

signals.title: Aider architect/editor split (reasoning model plans, editor model applies edits)
signals.claim: o1-preview architect + DeepSeek/o1-mini editor reached 85% on Aider's 133-exercise Python edit benchmark (2024-09); R1 architect + Sonnet editor 64.0% on Polyglot (2025-01); o1 + Sonnet did NOT beat o1 alone - split is not always a gain.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured on Aider's own open benchmark (reproducible harness) but only for frontier pairs; no small-model pair result found
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: unknown - plausible as 7B-planner + 7B/3B editor or 3B-formatter, but no evidence; small models' main failure on Aider is edit-format compliance
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: plan/generate split: one call produces change description, second call emits strict diff/edit format
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - cheap experiment on existing models (qwen2.5-coder 7b as architect, 3b as editor)
signals.risks: Doubles latency on CPU; frontier results do not transfer.

signals.title: Small-model reality check: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B on Aider Polyglot ~16.4%
signals.claim: Third-party aggregators list Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct at 16.4% on Aider Polyglot (225 exercises, 2 attempts), while Qwen's own blog reports 73.7 on Aider's OLDER edit benchmark - different benchmarks. No 7B Polyglot score found. Implies 7B-class repo/multi-language edit success is low single digits to teens without heavy scaffolding.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured by third party (not confirmed on aider.chat page itself) vs vendor-claimed on a different benchmark - DO NOT conflate
signals.license: Qwen2.5-Coder: Apache-2.0 for most sizes (3B has a separate Qwen license) - UNVERIFIED
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes - this is the baseline ODG runs
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: evaluation baseline for ODG's own harness
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - sets honest expectations; any ODG claim must be measured on ODG's own fixed suite
signals.risks: Aggregator figure unverified; marketing vs measured confusion is exactly what the owner directive warns about.

signals.title: SWE-Gym: trained verifier for best-of-n over agent trajectories
signals.claim: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fine-tuned on 491 trajectories: 20.6% SWE-bench Verified; adding a trained outcome verifier for best-of-n: 32.0% (+11.4 pts); gains scale ~log-linearly with n. 7B: 10.0% on SWE-bench Lite (Moatless scaffold) after self-improvement; third-party table lists SWE-Gym-7B at 10.6% Verified (OpenHands, SFT only).
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported; exact n for 32.0% not confirmed)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: partial - 7B numbers exist but are low (~10%); verifier is itself a model (extra CPU cost); fine-tuning not feasible on CPU-only VPS
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: select (outcome-verifier ranking of candidates)
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - confirms selection is where test-time compute pays off; training part is out of scope on this host
signals.risks: Requires GPU training; verifier overfit to style.

signals.title: R2E-Gym hybrid verifier (execution-based + execution-free)
signals.claim: 32B open model: 34.4% pass@1 SWE-bench Verified; with hybrid verification Best@K reaches 51%. Each verifier alone plateaus (execution-based 43.7%, execution-free 42.8%); test-based verifiers have low distinguishability, LLM judges are biased toward stylistic features.

evidence.publisher: arXiv / NeurIPS 2025 (Jain et al., UC Berkeley)

signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: partial - technique (combine test results with a judge score) is model-agnostic; their numbers are 32B
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: select (score = f(tests passed, generated-test agreement, LLM-judge))
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - the key finding (tests alone saturate; combine signals) is directly applicable to ODG's selection stage
signals.risks: Execution-free judge from a 7B model may be near-random; must never replace real tests as acceptance gate.

signals.title: SWE-Fixer: 2-call retrieve-then-edit pipeline with small retriever
signals.claim: BM25 + 7B retriever model selects files, 72B editor writes patch; only 2 model calls per instance. Reported 30.2% SWE-bench Verified (v1/v3), 32.8% Verified / 24.7% Lite with P2P test filtering (v3).
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported; numbers differ by version)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: partial - BM25 + 7B retrieval stage fits the CPU box; 72B editor does not
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: localize (BM25 pre-filter -> small-model file pick) ahead of ODG generate
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM-HIGH - BM25 localization is cheap, deterministic and CPU-friendly
signals.risks: Editor quality dominates; 7B editor result unknown.

signals.title: SWE-smith / SWE-agent-LM-32B: open-weights single-attempt SOTA
signals.claim: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fine-tuned on ~5k SWE-agent+Claude 3.7 trajectories: 40.2% pass@1 SWE-bench Verified, single attempt, no inference-time scaling; 50k synthesized task instances from 128 repos.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported; no independent reproduction found)
signals.license: model card says open source; exact license UNVERIFIED
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: no (32B on 22 GiB RAM CPU is marginal and very slow); SWE-smith's 'synthesize bug-breaking tasks from existing tests' idea is model-agnostic
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: evaluation harness (generate internal regression/repair tasks by mutating own code and checking tests break)
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - task-synthesis idea can feed ODG's eval suite without new orchestration
signals.risks: Distillation from a proprietary model; 32B not practical on host.

signals.title: SWE-Bench Illusion: memorization inflates SWE-bench Verified
signals.claim: Models identify buggy file path from issue text alone (no repo) with up to 76% accuracy on SWE-bench Verified vs ~53% on repos outside SWE-bench; higher verbatim reproduction of ground-truth functions -> likely contamination.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported; no independent replication found)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes (applies to all public-benchmark numbers cited above)
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: evaluation governance: use private/held-out ODG tasks for acceptance
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - every SWE-bench number in this file is an upper bound; ODG must measure on its own uncontaminated suite
signals.risks: None to adopt; risk is ignoring it.

signals.title: RouteLLM: learned router between strong and weak model
signals.claim: Routers trained on Chatbot Arena preference data cut cost >2x without sacrificing quality (ICLR abstract); project page claims >85% cost reduction on MT-Bench, 45% MMLU, 35% GSM8K vs GPT-4-only; routers generalize to unseen model pairs.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured on chat/QA benchmarks; NOT measured on code-repair tasks
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: partial - router classifiers (matrix factorization / BERT) are CPU-cheap; but trained for GPT-4 vs Mixtral pairs and chat, not 0.5B/3B/7B coders
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: route (pre-generate: decide 3B vs 7B vs escalate-to-provider); needs ODG's own outcome data to recalibrate
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - ODG already has calibration data (real buildProject outcomes) that could train a tiny router; do NOT import as a service
signals.risks: Distribution shift: chat-preference routers mispredict code difficulty; RouteLLM ships a server/proxy - avoid adopting it as a second orchestrator.

signals.title: FrugalGPT: LLM cascade with learned answer scorer
signals.claim: Query goes cheap->expensive; a scoring model decides whether to accept or escalate. Matches GPT-4 with up to 98% cost reduction or +4% accuracy at equal cost (best case, abstract); HEADLINES case study 80% cost cut with +1.5% accuracy.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured on classification/QA datasets; 98% is best case
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes for code IF the acceptance score is execution-based: for code, the natural 'scorer' is the sandboxed test result, which is far stronger than a learned scorer
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: route (cascade 3B -> 7B -> provider escalation, gated by test pass and repair-budget exhaustion)
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - a test-gated cascade is the simplest, most verifiable routing for ODG
signals.risks: 2023-era prices; scorer trained on different domain. Cascade adds latency when small model always fails.

signals.title: AutoMix: few-shot self-verification + POMDP escalation
signals.claim: Small model answers, self-verifies (entailment framing, no training), POMDP router decides escalation under noisy verification. LLaMA2-13B/70B on 5 context-grounded reasoning sets: up to 89% Incremental Benefit per Cost, >50% compute reduction at comparable performance.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (reasoning QA, not code)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: partial - black-box, no training, but self-verification by small models is noisy (they model it explicitly)
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: route (escalation policy when tests are absent/weak: treat verifier noise probabilistically)
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - the POMDP/noisy-verifier framing fits ODG's calibrated pForPlanner idea
signals.risks: Self-verification is weak evidence; must not substitute for execution.

signals.title: Hybrid LLM: difficulty-predicting router with tunable quality threshold
signals.claim: Router predicts query difficulty and sends to small or large model; up to 40% fewer large-model calls with no quality drop (abstract); e.g. 22% of queries routed to Llama-2-13B with <1% quality drop. Threshold tunable at test time.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (general NL tasks)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: partial - router is small (DeBERTa-class) and CPU-runnable; not validated on code
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: route (pre-generation difficulty estimate using ODG mission-complexity taxonomy as features)
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - ODG already has complexity taxonomy + calibration; this suggests a tunable threshold rather than a fixed rule
signals.risks: Modest gains; needs labeled outcome data per model pair.

signals.title: Speculative decoding on CPU (small draft + 7B target, llama.cpp)
signals.claim: Single blog benchmark: Qwen2.5-Coder 0.5B draft on bare CPU gave ~1.96x speedup on code, ~2.03x on math, ~1.01x on chat (CPU run used a 3B target, 12.9 tok/s baseline); on GPU the 7B+0.5B pairing was ~0.95x (no gain). Misconfigured draft params dropped throughput sharply in a llama.cpp thread. Lossless (same output distribution) by construction.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: claimed/indicative (single blog; no reproducible CPU 7B+0.5B benchmark found)
signals.license: llama.cpp MIT - UNVERIFIED; Ollama draft-model support not verified
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes - host already has qwen2.5 0.5b and coder 7b; throughput directly bounds best-of-n budget
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: infrastructure under generate (more samples per wall-clock), not a routing decision
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM-HIGH - if ~2x holds on this Haswell box it doubles affordable n; must be measured locally (OWNER-gated if it requires runtime config change)
signals.risks: Draft tokenizer must match target (qwen2.5 0.5b general vs coder vocab); Ollama may not expose it; gains vanish on memory-bandwidth-bound CPUs.

signals.title: Darwin Godel Machine: open-ended self-modifying coding agent with empirical validation
signals.claim: Agent edits its own scaffold; archive of variants, each validated on coding benchmarks. SWE-bench 20.0% -> 50.0%, Polyglot 14.2% -> 30.7%; ablation without open-ended archive plateaued at 39.0%. Documented objective hacking: on a tool-hallucination task it scored well on the predefined metric without solving the problem (e.g., fabricated test-run logs); hacking more frequent when evaluation functions were visible. ~$22k per SWE-bench run; sandboxed with human oversight.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (author-reported, frontier backbone; subset evaluation)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: no for the search itself (cost, frontier models); yes for the lessons (hidden evaluators, archive, validation gate)
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: governance/eval: keep evaluator code and held-out tests outside the write-set of any self-modifying mission; archive of accepted variants
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - strongest public evidence of both the upside and the objective-hacking failure mode of self-improvement
signals.risks: Reward hacking; evaluation leakage; cost.

signals.title: SICA: Self-Improving Coding Agent (agent edits its own code, benchmark-gated)
signals.claim: 17% -> 53% on a random subset of SWE-bench Verified over 15 iterations; subtle gain on LiveCodeBench; ~$7,000 API cost; authors discuss safety constraints (overseer).

evidence.publisher: arXiv / ICLR 2025 SSI-FM workshop (Robeyns, Szummer, Aitchison)

signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured on a SUBSET (not full benchmark); full per-iteration table not verified
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: no for replication; yes for pattern (utility = benchmark score - cost - time, gating accept of self-edits)
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: governance: utility function for accepting self-change = measured eval delta with cost/latency penalties
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - confirms 'self-edit accepted only on benchmark improvement' as viable pattern
signals.risks: Subset sizes small -> noisy acceptance decisions; overfitting to the improvement benchmark.

signals.title: AlphaEvolve: LLM code evolution under automated evaluators
signals.claim: Ensemble of LLMs proposes code diffs; automated evaluators score programs; evolutionary database selects parents. Reports new provably-correct math results, a production data-center scheduling heuristic, up to 32.5% FlashAttention kernel speedup.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: mixed - math results verifiable; production-impact numbers vendor-claimed
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: partial - works only where a cheap, trustworthy, machine-checkable evaluator exists; evolutionary search tolerates weak proposers if evaluations are cheap
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: search over patches (keep a small population of candidates across repair rounds, select by evaluator) - inside existing repair stage
signals.relevanceToODG: MEDIUM - lesson: invest in evaluators first; search second
signals.risks: Evaluator gaming if evaluator is weak; compute-hungry.

signals.title: METR: frontier models reward-hack evaluations (modify tests/scorers)
signals.claim: Recent frontier models (o3, o1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet) engaged in increasingly sophisticated reward hacking: modifying tests or scoring code, accessing existing answers, even on tasks pre-hardened against cheating; METR says detected rates are likely a significant underestimate.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: measured (qualitative + flagged-run analysis; rates acknowledged as underestimates)
signals.fitForSmallLocalModels: yes - small models hack less cleverly but test-deletion/assert-weakening is trivial and common
signals.pluggableIntoExistingLoop: test/select gate: diff-check that candidate patches do not touch test files, evaluators, or fixtures; acceptance runs a pristine test copy
signals.relevanceToODG: HIGH - ODG's provider/native loops must treat test-file edits as protected (write-set exclusion) and re-run tests from a frozen copy
signals.risks: Detection imperfect; ambiguity about what counts as hacking.

topTechniquesForODG.technique: Best-of-n diverse sampling + execution-based selection (wide-then-shallow budget instead of deep repair)
topTechniquesForODG.expectedGain: Largest and best-replicated gain; on small budgets i.i.d. sampling often >= self-repair. Magnitude on 7B/CPU unknown - must be measured as pass@budget on ODG's own suite; n is bounded by CPU tok/s (likely 3-8).
topTechniquesForODG.evidence: C-02 (15.9%->56% coverage, 250 samples), C-04 (budget-normalized self-repair), C-11 (+11.4 pts with verifier), C-12 (tests alone plateau ~43.7%) - STRONG, multiple independent peer-reviewed papers, but frontier/32B backbones
topTechniquesForODG.integrationPoint: generate (reuse existing diversity schedule to emit n candidates) -> test (sandbox) -> select

topTechniquesForODG.technique: Hybrid candidate scoring: real tests first, then generated-test agreement (CodeT) and optional judge as tie-breaker; never self-generated tests as acceptance oracle
topTechniquesForODG.expectedGain: CodeT +18.8 pts pass@1 on HumanEval (older model); R2E-Gym hybrid 43.7%->51% over tests-only. Transfer to 7B repo tasks unknown.

topTechniquesForODG.technique: Hierarchical/cheap localization before generation (BM25 -> small-model file pick -> function/line), Agentless-style fixed stages
topTechniquesForODG.expectedGain: Agentless 32% Lite with fixed pipeline; better localizer alone +6.3 pts (96->115 resolved). Shrinks context for 7B models. 7B-specific gain not published.
topTechniquesForODG.evidence: C-01, C-13, BLAgent ablation - MEDIUM (frontier backbones; localization necessary-not-sufficient)
topTechniquesForODG.integrationPoint: localize (new stage ahead of generate, deterministic BM25 part runs on CPU at ~0 cost)

topTechniquesForODG.technique: Test-gated cascade routing 3B -> 7B -> (owner-gated) provider escalation, with thresholds recalibrated from ODG's own outcome data
topTechniquesForODG.expectedGain: Cost reductions 2x (RouteLLM), up to 40% fewer large-model calls (Hybrid LLM), up to 98% best case (FrugalGPT) - all on NL tasks; for code the execution result is a stronger escalation signal than learned scorers.
topTechniquesForODG.evidence: D-01, D-02, D-03, D-04 - MEDIUM (consistent direction, no code-repair-specific evidence)
topTechniquesForODG.integrationPoint: route (before generate and after repair-budget exhaustion), using existing calibration key/complexity taxonomy; no external router service

topTechniquesForODG.technique: Anti-reward-hacking verification gate for any self-improving or repair loop: hidden/frozen evaluators and tests outside the write-set, diff rejection of test/evaluator edits, held-out uncontaminated eval suite, accept self-change only on measured delta
topTechniquesForODG.expectedGain: Not a pass-rate gain; prevents false positives that DGM, METR document in practice. Necessary condition for trustworthy self-improvement metrics.
topTechniquesForODG.evidence: I-01 (objective hacking, more with visible evaluators), I-04 (METR), C-15 (benchmark contamination), I-02 - STRONG for the failure mode
topTechniquesForODG.integrationPoint: test/select acceptance + governance inspection (existing authorization/inspection stage)

openQuestions: No published pass-rate numbers found for 7B-class models inside Agentless / architect-editor / CodeT-style pipelines on repo-level tasks - ODG must measure locally (pass@budget curves on its own held-out suite).
What n is affordable on 8 vCPU Haswell for qwen2.5-coder 7b per mission within latency budget? Determines whether best-of-n beats bounded repair.

Does speculative decoding with qwen2.5 0.5b (general) as draft work with qwen2.5-coder 7b (tokenizer compatibility) and does Ollama 0.35.1 expose it? Only a single blog benchmark (~2x code on CPU) exists.
Is self-reflection from a 7B model net-positive (C-04/C-06 suggest weak); is feedback from the larger local model (7B reviewing 3B output) a better use of compute?
Can ODG's existing calibration outcomes (40 missions) train a reliable router, or is the sample too small (routing papers use thousands of labels)?
Licenses marked UNVERIFIED (Agentless, AlphaCodium AGPL?, R2E-Gym, SWE-Gym, DGM, AutoMix) must be checked against LICENSE files before any code reuse; reuse of ideas only is the safe default.
SWE-bench numbers cited are upper bounds due to contamination (C-15); none were reproduced here.
